title: Lung rehabilitation (after pneumonia, with COPD)
what: These are sessions that teach you to breathe more easily and move more. They include exercises, breathing practice and everyday tips.
why: After pneumonia, or with long-term lung disease, when shortness of breath gets in the way of walking and work.
duration: a session usually takes 45 to 90 minutes; a course usually lasts several weeks
tell_doctor: How much shortness of breath affects daily life
Which inhalers and medicines you use
Whether you need oxygen at home

prepare.title: Check-up
prepare.text: Before the course, your breathing and heart are usually checked, and sometimes a walking test is done.

prepare.title: Inhalers
prepare.text: Do not stop on your own. Use them as usual and bring them with you.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not eat a heavy meal 1 to 2 hours before the session.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes and comfortable sports shoes.

bring: Your inhalers and a list of medicines
steps: The doctor asks how you feel and checks the oxygen in your blood
You learn to breathe slowly and through pursed lips
Walking or exercise bike at a pace you can manage
You are shown how to cope with an attack of breathlessness
You get an exercise plan for home
feel: You may feel short of breath during exercise. The pace is set to suit you
Muscles may ache after the first sessions
After a few weeks, walking usually gets easier
after: Exercise at home following the plan between visits
Quitting smoking helps your lungs a lot
Move every day and increase the effort little by little
red_flags: Breathlessness does not ease at rest, lips turn blue: call your local emergency number
Chest pain: call your local emergency number
Fever above 38 and your cough gets worse

faq.q: Can I exercise if I get very breathless?
faq.a: Yes, the sessions are matched to your condition. The load is raised gradually.

faq.q: Do I need to keep going after the course?
faq.a: Yes. If you stop exercising, the improvement slowly fades.

reminders.text: Lung rehabilitation today. Bring your inhalers, water and sports shoes.
